# Chih-Yu Lin

::: {.hero-subtitle}
Ph.D. Candidate, National Taiwan University  
Visiting Researcher, University of Oulu
:::

I design wireless communication systems that are aware of **timeliness**, **task utility**, and **resource constraints**. My research focuses on 6G wireless networks, task-oriented semantic communication, integrated sensing and communication, Age of Information, NOMA, vehicular networks, and learning-based resource allocation.

## Research vision

Future wireless networks will not only deliver bits. They will support sensing, inference, control, and decision-making under strict timeliness and resource constraints. My research asks three connected questions: *what* should be transmitted, *when* should information be updated, and *how* should wireless resources be shared. See [Research](research.qmd) for details.

## Background

Before my Ph.D., I worked as an engineer at TSMC and ASMedia, on semiconductor design workflows and high-speed USB4 IP solutions. This industry experience shapes how I approach wireless systems research: with attention to implementation constraints, not only theoretical performance. My full trajectory is on the [CV](cv.qmd) page.
